## Methods and Technical Skills

**Programming and tools:** Python (pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Streamlit), R (reading and translating analysis code), Jupyter, Salesforce

**Statistical methods:** mixed-effects models, generalized estimating equations, OLS with robust standard errors, multiple imputation, multiple-comparison correction, binary and multinomial logistic regression, principal component analysis, cluster analysis

**Measurement:** multi-item scale scoring, variable crosswalks across data dictionaries, cross-language instrument and program adaptation

**Languages:** English, Korean (native/bilingual)

## Research and Data Experience

::: {.cv-entry}
[Research Assistant]{.role}
[Aug 2026–Present]{.dates}

Human Flourishing Program, Harvard University

::: {.cv-entry}
[Summer Research Intern]{.role}
[Jun–Aug 2026]{.dates}
:::
::: {.org}
Lee Kum Sheung Center for Health and Happiness, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health<br>
Mentors: Richard Cowden PhD, Tyler VanderWeele PhD
:::

- Conduct the South Africa site analysis of the REACH Forgiveness randomized controlled trial (RCT), a multisite intervention study of forgiveness and well-being.
- Translate the Indonesia site's R analysis pipeline (about 4,000 lines) into documented, reproducible Python.
- Build the South Africa analytic dataset, including a variable crosswalk against the site data dictionary, 17 multi-item scale composites, and a 2,745-row longitudinal panel.
- Fit random-intercept mixed-effects models for all preregistered outcomes with Holm-Bonferroni correction.
- Implement multiple imputation and generalized estimating equations (GEE), then OLS with robust standard errors under documented protocol deviations from the preregistration.
- Model attrition to assess missing-data assumptions and workbook engagement as a predictor of forgiveness outcomes.
- Write the results and discussion sections of the South Africa site manuscript.

- Synthesize analytical findings from visualizations into reports that inform strategies for expanding the ScratchJr program's global reach.
